goal: Make agent-kit's validate check finish sooner. Its runs don't queue (they start within seconds on a hosted runner); about 90% of each run is one serial unit-test step.
changed: quality.py record --workers N runs the suite in N children; each claims the next free test through an O_EXCL file in a shared temporary folder, and the parent merges the rows, the completeness and the exit status.
WorkersTest in tests/test_quality.py: once-each recording, real concurrency, more children than tests, a child cut short, bad usage.
make record takes RECORD_WORKERS; validate.yml passes $(nproc).
bstack 0.59.0 in kit.yaml and changes.yaml, the qualitydirector SKILL.md, and the generated files.

claims.claim: With --workers the recorder records every test exactly once, with the same outcomes as one child, and keeps the completeness and exit rules.
claims.check: WorkersTest passes and fails on three broken recorders; five full parallel runs of this suite recorded each test id once with no failures.

claims.claim: One worker (the default) behaves as before.
claims.check: tests.test_quality passes, including ParityTest and InterpreterFlagsTest.

claims.claim: The validate unit-test step is faster on the hosted runner.
claims.check: Needs this PR's validate run; baseline is the step's median of about 167 s over recent runs.
claims.remaining: Read the step time on this PR's validate run and on the next few pushes to main.

next.item: Trim the slowest tests: test_weekly_claude_code.WeeklyJob, test_quality.ParityTest and test_quality.InterpreterFlagsTest.
next.source: inferred from the CI test records
next.why_now: With tests spread over every core, the longest single tests set the floor of the step.
next.impact: Each agent-kit PR's validate check finishes sooner again, and keeps doing so as the suite grows.

release.note: bstack 0.59.0: quality.py record --workers N runs a unittest suite in N children that share the tests as they go, and agent-kit's validate check records its tests with one worker per core.
